subject: Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class data.table

messages.author: cc5b93d906a30573
messages.subject: Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class data.table
parts:
I'm not sure if this is more a general R question or specific to
ggplot2, but any
help would be appreciated here.

I am unable to use a data.table (my preferred data structure) in place
of a data.frame
as an argument to ggplot(). Here is an example:

> library('data.table')
> v <- data.table(a=c(1,2,3,4),b=c(5,8,9,10))
> ggplot(v) + geom_point(aes(a,b))
Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class data.table

Besides the very verbose "ggplot(as.data.frame(v))" is there a simple
way to
remedy this problem (e.g. through some sort of implicit conversion)?

With thanks,
Dan

> of a data.frame
> as an argument to ggplot().  Here is an example:
>
> > library('data.table')
> > v <- data.table(a=c(1,2,3,4),b=c(5,8,9,10))
> > ggplot(v) + geom_point(aes(a,b))
>
> Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class data.table
>
> Besides the very verbose "ggplot(as.data.frame(v))" is there a simple
> way to
> remedy this problem (e.g. through some sort of implicit conversion)?

ggplot2 can do implicit conversions that you want using the fortify
function. If a fortify function for the data type you have exists, it
will be used to try and turn the data into a data.frame. If you
create a function:

fortify.data.table <- function(model, data, ...) as.data.frame(model)

then

ggplot(v) + geom_point(aes(a,b))

will work.

> With thanks,
> Dan

--Brian Diggs

> create a function:

Since data tables are very close to data frames, you might try:

ggplot.data.table <- ggplot.data.frame

As long as all the correct methods are supported that should work
without having to create another copy of the data.
